queue.what: the order the enrichers run in. Ordering is a decision, not folklore: every enricher sees the volume as the ones before it left it, so what is written here is what a reader has to know to predict a build. A name here that no enricher answers to fails the build, and so does an enricher the binary offers that is not named here.

why.merge: first, because everything after it should see the whole volume: a collection folded in from another reading is a collection that wants an icon and a score like any other.
why.national: after merge, so a feature contributed by another reading can also learn which subwatershed its ground lies in.
why.stdicons: after merge, which is the whole reason it is post-composition: a merged-in collection that declares a standard icon resolves it too.
why.lenses: last, because a picture attaches to a ground, and the grounds are not all known until everything that could contribute one has run.

merge.what: the resolution distances, in world pixels of the 8192-pixel square, and the per-key attribute policy. A confirmed match needs the same name near where the alignment predicts; beyond twice the radius the same name is a different place bearing it; between the two the resolution declines to decide.

attributes.what: which side of a matched feature wins, key by key. Anything unlisted is serving-wins: what the serving reading says stands. donor-fills-empty is the enrichment rule the description pioneered -- the serving side keeps what it has and takes only what it lacks -- and every take is ledgered by key.

national.what: which collections a national evidence base contributed to a volume. The membership join never makes a claim about a feature of one of these: the hydrography is the evidence, and a subwatershed does not need a sentence telling it which subwatershed it lies in.
